blocks.text: Some functional groups can absorb energy from sunlight in the form of ultraviolet light. Polymers with such groups can be degraded by light and are called photodegradable. Some polymers with carbonyl groups (C=O) in their chains have been developed because they absorb UV strongly. The absorbed UV light weakens bonds within the chains and the forces between chains, which makes the polymer more biodegradable and speeds up its breakdown into less toxic compounds in the environment.
However, photodegradable plastics cannot be used for long, and recycling them is not efficient. Also, most plastic is buried in landfills, where there is no light for photodegradation.
